lead: A load cell is a spring with a measuring circuit. A shaped metal or alloy element takes the force, and bonded strain gauges turn its small stretch or squeeze into a resistance change. A full bridge makes that change a millivolt signal, calibrated directly in newtons or kilograms. The same idea measures torque when the gauges sit at 45° on a shaft. Load cells weigh trucks at toll plazas, stop cranes from overloading, and check motor power on test beds; torque measurement sets bolt tension and checks pumps.
prereq: You need Chapter 2.2 for gauge factor, bridge configurations and temperature compensation.

blocks.text: The elastic element is the metal part that carries the load. Its shape sets where strain appears, how uniform it is, and how much output the bridge gives. The element stays below its yield point, so it returns to zero when the load is removed.

items: Column: a solid or hollow post in compression or tension. Simple and stiff; used in weighbridges and silo scales.
Cantilever and double-bending beam: a beam bends under load. Common in small retail scales and platform scales.
Shear web: a thin web carries shear; gauges read shear strain. Gives good rejection of off-centre load.
Proving ring: a ring deflects under load; used as a reference standard.
S-type: shaped like an S, works in tension or compression; used for crane hooks and hoppers.

blocks.text: Four active gauges form a full bridge. Two gauges see tension and two see compression, so their resistance changes add in the bridge. The full bridge also cancels the effect of uniform temperature change, because all gauges move together.

blocks.where: V_o is bridge output in V; V_s is excitation voltage in V; GF is gauge factor (dimensionless); ε is strain in the element (dimensionless, often µε). This is for four active gauges of equal strain magnitude; a quarter bridge gives one quarter of this output.

blocks.text: A load cell is sold by its ratings. The rated capacity is the maximum load for which the output is specified. Safe overload is a higher load the cell can take occasionally without damage. Ultimate overload is the load that may cause permanent change; never use it as a working limit.

head: Term
Meaning
rows: Occasional load above capacity without damage, often 150% of capacity.
Load that can damage the cell, often 300% of capacity.
Slow output change under a steady load.
Difference between loading and unloading output at the same load.
Largest deviation from a straight-line output.
Full-load output in mV per V of excitation; about 2 mV/V typical.

blocks.text: Mechanical stops limit travel under overload. Hermetic sealing keeps moisture out of the gauge area. A stainless-steel or IP-rated body is normal for wash-down scales. Hydraulic load cells use a piston and pressure gauge; capacitive types use plate spacing; piezoelectric types use quartz charge. Each has a place, but the bonded strain-gauge cell is the common choice for static weight.

Torque is a twisting moment. A force F at radius r gives torque T = F · r. On a shaft, the surface is in shear, and the principal strains lie at 45° to the axis. Gauges are bonded along those 45° directions, not along the axis, to get the largest signal.

blocks.where: T is torque in N·m; F is force in N; r is radius in m.
P is shaft power in W; N is speed in rev/min; T is torque in N·m. If N is in rev/s, use P = 2π N T.

blocks.text: A full bridge on the shaft uses four gauges at ±45°. It adds the tension and compression changes and cancels bending and axial strain. The bridge output is still a few millivolts, so an amplifier sits close to the shaft or on the stator.

items: Slip rings: metal brushes touch rotating rings. Simple, but wear and contact noise.
Rotary transformer: a rotating winding is coupled magnetically to a fixed winding. No contact, good for continuous running.
FM telemetry: a small transmitter on the shaft sends a frequency-modulated signal to a fixed receiver. No contact, robust, higher cost.

blocks.text: A stationary frame can measure reaction torque: mount the motor or pump on bearings and measure the restraining force at a known radius. This avoids rotating electronics. Applications include motor and pump test beds, torque wrench calibration, and drive-shaft monitoring.

figure.caption: The numbers are the worked example: 10 kN on a 20 mm steel column gives 159 µε and only 1.59 mV at the bridge, so an amplifier follows.

spec.aria: A chain of blocks from the applied load, through the elastic column and its strain, to the bonded gauges, the bridge output and the display.

examples.question: A compression load cell is a solid steel column of 20 mm diameter with E = 200 GPa. Four 120 Ω gauges of gauge factor 2.0 form a full bridge excited at 5 V. For a 10 kN load find the stress, the strain, ΔR per gauge and the bridge output. Use the full-bridge relation for four active gauges of equal strain magnitude.
steps: Resistance change per gauge: ΔR = GF·ε·R = 2.0 × 1.59×10⁻⁴ × 120 Ω = 0.038 Ω.
Bridge output: V_o = V_s·GF·ε = 5 V × 2.0 × 1.59×10⁻⁴ = 1.59×10⁻³ V = 1.59 mV.
examples.answer: The stress is 31.8 MPa, the strain is 159 µε, each gauge changes by 0.038 Ω, and the full bridge gives 1.59 mV at 5 V excitation.
examples.check:
import math
d = 0.020
r = d / 2
A = round(math.pi * r * r, 7)
sigma_MPa = round(10000 / A / 1e6, 1)
eps = sigma_MPa * 1e6 / 200e9
micro = int(round(eps * 1e6))
dR = round(2.0 * eps * 120, 3)
Vo_mV = round(5 * 2.0 * eps * 1000, 2)
print(A)
print(sigma_MPa)
print(micro)
print(dR)
print(Vo_mV)

traps: Using the quarter-bridge formula for a four-active-gauge load cell. That under-reads by a factor of four.
Confusing rated capacity with safe overload and ultimate overload. Rated capacity is the specified working load; safe overload is an occasional higher load; ultimate overload may damage the cell.
Bonding torque gauges along the shaft axis. Torsion gives principal strains at 45° to the axis, so axial gauges see little useful strain.
Reading sensitivity as output volts instead of millivolts per volt of excitation. A 2 mV/V cell at 5 V gives only 10 mV at full load.
Forgetting that a four-gauge full bridge already includes temperature compensation; adding a separate compensation resistor can spoil the calibration.

quiz.a: An elastic element with bonded strain gauges in a bridge, calibrated to read force or weight.

quiz.q: Why use four active gauges instead of one?
quiz.a: A full bridge gives about four times the quarter-bridge output and cancels uniform temperature change, because all gauges move together.

quiz.q: Define rated capacity and safe overload for a load cell.
quiz.a: Rated capacity is the maximum load for which output is specified. Safe overload is an occasional higher load the cell can take without damage.

quiz.q: A steel column of 20 mm diameter has E = 200 GPa and carries 10 kN. Find the axial strain in µε.
A full bridge has GF = 2.0, strain 200 µε and excitation 10 V. Find the output.
Why are torque gauges placed at 45° to the shaft axis?
quiz.a: Torsion produces principal strains at ±45° to the axis. Gauges along those directions get maximum strain; gauges along the axis get almost none.

quiz.q: Compare slip rings and FM telemetry for a rotating torque shaft.
quiz.a: Slip rings are simple and cheap but wear and add contact noise. FM telemetry has no contact, lasts longer, and is more robust, at higher cost and complexity.

beyond: Not for the exam. Load cells are moving to MEMS and thin-film gauges for small medical and robot joints, while wireless torque telemetry is common on wind-turbine shafts and electric-vehicle drivetrains. Search for load cell creep, torque telemetry, and strain-gauge load cell IP rating to see datasheet language. The same bridge ideas return in pressure and force sensors in later units.
